device.description: 10-bit single-channel voltage-output DAC with I2C interface
device.note: dac101c081.pdf (SNVS801B) p.4 pin configuration and functions, p.6 recommended operating conditions, p.10 timing (toutz), p.15 power-on reset, p.19 slave addresses (Table 1) and writing, p.20 reading and DAC register (Figure 26)

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: internal: PD1:PD0 of the DAC register (bits 13:12)

commands.name: Write DAC register
commands.note: two data bytes: X X PD1 PD0 then the data; VOUT updates at the ACK after the lower byte; repeated byte pairs before STOP write again

pages: p.4 (pins), p.6 (ROC: VA 2.7-5.5 V, digital inputs 0-5.5 V regardless of VA), p.10 (timing, toutz max 270 ns fast mode), p.15 (power-on reset), p.16 (power-down), p.19 (Table 1 addresses, Figure 24 write), p.20 (Figure 25 read, Figure 26 register X X PD1 PD0 D9..D0 0 0)
notModeled: analog output, reference (VA, or VREF on the VSSOP DAC1x1C085), power-down output terminations and wake-up time

address pins are three-level (GND, VA, floating or VA/2): the floating-pin addresses (ADR0 float: 0x0C; ADR1 float row and ADR1/ADR0 float combinations) cannot be expressed; SCL/SDA ties are not documented (null)
broadcast address 1001000 (0x48), to which every DAC1x1C08x responds and updates, is not modeled (one address per part)
the address pins are sampled until the first non-broadcast access and then locked until power cycle
Hs-mode (3.4 MHz) entry; toutz uses the fast-mode maximum (270 ns)
power-on requires VA to drop below 200 mV for a reset
Table 1 lists a second address after each slave address (e.g. '0001101, 1000110'); it is the 'do not use' companion address of the DAC121C08x datasheet and is not modeled
variants: DAC101C081Q and DAC101C085 (VSSOP-8 with ADR1 and VREF) in the same datasheet; DAC101C085 has no orderable part in the skeleton
